Comment generation latency grows linearly with the number of issues. Get the environment for all issues in one batched query, e.g. from the existing top-issues Snuba query.

The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion checks use truthiness (`self.initial_data.get("age")` / `.get("timestamp")`), so a report with `age: 0` plus a `timestamp` passes validation. That breaks the intended rule that a report follows only one spec, and `age: 0` is a realistic value because age counts milliseconds since the report was created. Check for the key instead, e.g. `if "age" in self.initial_data` / `if "timestamp" in self.initial_data` (or `is not None`).

sms-workflow-reminder-retry-count-tracki.texto: The `retryCount > 1` branch of the OR is not limited to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`, so the SMS cron deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1, whatever its method (EMAIL/WHATSAPP) or scheduled state. Once any other path increments retryCount, this cron will silently delete those reminders. Move `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` outside the OR, or add it (plus `scheduled: false`) to the retryCount branch.

The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` inside the catch block has no error handling of its own, so if it throws (for example the row was already deleted, or a DB error) the exception escapes the for-loop. The remaining reminders in that cron run are skipped and the handler returns a 500. Wrap the retryCount update in its own try/catch, or use `updateMany` with the id so a missing row does not throw.

The new OR branch filters only on `retryCount`, which has no index (the only matching index is (method, scheduled, scheduledDate)). The OR therefore likely forces a full sequential scan of the WorkflowReminder table on every cron run. Scope the branch with `method: SMS, scheduled: false` so the existing composite index can be used, or add an index that covers retryCount.

span-buffer-multiprocess-enhancement-wit.texto: Processes are created with `get_context("spawn").Process`, which is `SpawnProcess`, and `SpawnProcess` is not a subclass of `multiprocessing.Process`, so `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is always false and an unhealthy flusher is never killed. A hung process keeps running alongside the replacement started by `_create_process_for_shards`, so two processes flush the same shards at once (possible duplicate segments, leaked processes). Check `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess)`, or skip only `threading.Thread`, before calling `kill()`.

In `join`, once the deadline has passed the loop `break`s, so `terminate()` is skipped for every process after that point. Those flusher processes keep running against Redis after the consumer has shut down or rebalanced. Replace the `break` with skipping only the wait, and still terminate every process.

`get_memory_info` is `iter_cluster_memory_usage(self.client)`, which reads memory for the whole Redis cluster, so calling it once per shard buffer queries the same cluster N times on every `submit`. This adds N-1 redundant cluster-wide round-trips per submit and gives the same ratio, because used and available are both multiplied by N. Call `get_memory_info()` once on a single buffer/client, as the old code did.

The test patches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None` at line 15, so the added `time.sleep(0.1)` returns immediately and gives the flusher thread no time to run. `step.join()` then sets `stopped` while the flusher may not have flushed yet, so `(msg,) = messages` can fail intermittently. Wait for the messages to arrive with a bounded poll loop, or save the real `time.sleep` before patching and use that.

The `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` timer is tagged `shards`, but the other per-process flusher metrics in the same loop (`spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes`) use `shard`. Because of this, dashboards and alerts that filter or group by `shard` will not split this timer by shard as they do the other two. Rename the tag to `{"shard": shard_tag}`.

unified-storage-performance-optimization.texto: The new log line calls s.search.TotalDocs(), and bleveBackend.TotalDocs (bleve.go:144) loops over b.cache without holding cacheMu. It runs after the watch goroutine has started (line 207), and that goroutine can call getOrCreateIndex -> BuildIndex -> `b.cache[key] = idx` at the same time, which can crash the process with a fatal 'concurrent map iteration and map write' error. Fix: take b.cacheMu.RLock() inside TotalDocs, or compute the total before starting the event goroutine.

BuildIndex used to hold cacheMu for its whole body, which serialized the errgroup workers in searchSupport.init. Now they run in parallel and all assign to the captured outer `err` (`_, _, err = s.build(...)`; `return err` at search.go:190), so one worker can overwrite another worker's failure with nil before it is returned. A failed index build can then be silently dropped and startup reports success. Fix: in init, use a goroutine-local variable (`_, _, err := s.build(...)`) and make totalBatchesIndexed atomic.
